sources.title: 6.685 Electric Machines — Class Notes 2: Magnetic Circuit Basics
verifiedClaims: Magnetic flux is the surface integral of B; flux entering a junction equals flux leaving it.
The magnetoquasistatic Ampere loop integral of H equals enclosed free current; a linked N-turn winding supplies NI ampere-turns.
A uniform small air gap has reluctance g/(mu0 A), neglecting fringing.
Series sections carry the same flux; their MMF drops add.
Right-hand orientation determines the signs of current and the magnetic contour.
sources.license: MIT OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 except otherwise noted; document copyright James L. Kirtley Jr. 2003.
sources.use: Equation and concept verification; no copied figure.

sources.title: 6.061 Introduction to Electric Power Systems — Chapter 6: Magnetic Circuit Analog to Electric Circuits
verifiedClaims: Uniform linear segments have reluctance l/(mu A).
Fringing occurs near a gap; the no-fringing approximation is best for small gaps and generally overestimates gap reluctance.
A symmetric pair of parallel gaps each carries half the common-path flux.
For a linear one-winding magnetic circuit with fully linked flux, lambda=N Phi and L=N^2/R_total.
The inductor terminal voltage under passive sign convention is d(lambda)/dt.
sources.license: MIT OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 except otherwise noted; document copyright James L. Kirtley Jr. 2003.
sources.use: Equation and assumption verification; no copied figure.

sources.title: 6.061 Introduction to Electric Power Systems — Chapter 8: Electromagnetic Forces and Loss Mechanisms
verifiedClaims: Ferromagnetic B-H behavior is nonlinear and history-dependent; remanence and coercivity characterize a hysteresis loop.
For a specified cycle, loss per unit material volume equals the loop integral of H dB.
Thin steel laminations reduce eddy-current loss; increased resistivity also helps.
For sinusoidal, fully penetrating flux parallel to a thin sheet, classical eddy loss density scales with frequency squared, peak flux density squared, and sheet thickness squared.
Measured material loss data are needed for practical prediction; incremental permeability is dB/dH.
sources.license: MIT OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 except third-party material. Steel data/graphs are credited to U.S. Steel and used by permission; do not copy those graphs.
sources.use: Physics verification only; no empirical curves reproduced.

sources.title: 6.622 Power Electronics — Lecture 9: Magnetics, Part 1 (typed notes)
verifiedClaims: For fixed linear geometry, L=N^2 mu A/l and lambda=L i.
With a gap, total reluctance includes both core and air-gap terms.
When gap reluctance dominates, inductance is less sensitive to core permeability.
For a linear gapped structure, much of the magnetic field energy can reside in the gap.
sources.license: MIT OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 except otherwise noted.
sources.use: Cross-check only. Typed transcription contains typographical errors; use verified physical definitions rather than copying its wording.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, section 12.7: Magnetism in Matter
verifiedClaims: Domains can rotate and aligned domains can grow under an applied magnetic field.
Ferromagnetic response saturates and depends on previous magnetization.
Remanent magnetization may remain after the applied field is removed.
Magnetic field lines form closed loops.
sources.license: Current web edition states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; third-party elements may have separate notices.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, section 13.1: Faraday’s Law
verifiedClaims: Phi is the surface integral of B dot n dA.
Induced emf around an oriented closed loop is minus the time derivative of linked magnetic flux.
A stationary field with fixed geometry does not generate a Faraday emf.
sources.license: Current web edition states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

sources.title: University Physics Volume 2, section 14.2: Self-Inductance and Inductors
verifiedClaims: For a linear coil with common linked flux, N Phi=L I.
Self-induced emf opposes change in current, not necessarily current itself.
A constant current gives zero self-induced emf for fixed geometry and material state.

sources.title: Using Differential Inductance and Coils in COMSOL Multiphysics
sources.pages: A Brief Review of the Theory; published July 15, 2024
verifiedClaims: When flux linkage is a single-valued function of instantaneous current, differential inductance is its derivative with respect to current; secant inductance is the flux-linkage/current ratio.
These coincide for a linear coil with no bias flux; the chain rule connects differential inductance to the time derivative of current.

claims.claim: Conventional current fixes magnetic-field orientation through the right-hand rule. Reversing current reverses the field.
claims.equations: ∮ H·dl = Σ signed Nₖiₖ
claims.qualification: Magnetostatic / magnetoquasistatic model. Animated marks indicate field direction, not moving magnetic particles.

claims.claim: For a uniform mean path, the loop equation reduces to Hl=Ni; for a toroid H depends on radius.
claims.equations: H ≈ Ni/l; H(r) = Ni/(2πr)
claims.qualification: A mean-path rectangular-core approximation is different from an exact full-field solution.

claims.claim: H is magnetic field intensity, B is flux density, Φ is magnetic flux and λ is flux linkage.
claims.equations: B = μH; μ = μ₀μᵣ; Φ = ∫ B·dA; λ = NΦ
claims.qualification: B=μH uses a linear constitutive model. λ=NΦ assumes the same flux links every turn.

claims.claim: For uniform normal flux, Φ=BA. The quantities have different physical units and must not be conflated.
claims.equations: H: A/m; B: T; Φ: Wb; λ: Wb-turn; μ: H/m; 1 cm² = (10⁻² m)² = 10⁻⁴ m²
claims.qualification: Use Φ=BA only for the stated uniform-field approximation. Apply the square to the centimeter conversion factor as well as the length unit.

claims.claim: The course calculation value of vacuum permeability is an excellent instructional approximation.
claims.equations: μ₀ ≈ 4π × 10⁻⁷ H/m
claims.qualification: The approximation sign avoids treating this as an exact modern SI defining constant.

claims.claim: A winding supplies MMF Ni; a uniform linear segment has reluctance l/(μA).
claims.equations: ℱ = Ni; ℜ = l/(μA); Φ = ℱ/ℜ
claims.qualification: Reluctance is not an electrical resistance and its presence does not itself imply Joule loss.

claims.claim: Series magnetic sections share flux; MMF drops add. Branch fluxes obey continuity at a junction.
claims.equations: Σ ℱ = Σ Φⱼℜⱼ; Σ signed Φⱼ = 0
claims.qualification: No leakage is included in the lumped circuit. Use the correct topology before summing reluctances.

claims.claim: Core and gap reluctances add along one series flux path; their MMF drops can differ greatly.
claims.equations: ℜc = lc/(μ₀μᵣAc); ℜg = g/(μ₀Ag); Ni = Hc lc + Hg g
claims.qualification: The core’s μᵣ must not be inserted into the air-gap reluctance.

claims.claim: Fringing spreads the field near a gap. Equal gap and core face areas are a simplifying approximation.
claims.equations: Φ = BcAc = BgAg
claims.qualification: The simulator uses Ag=Ac and neglects fringing/leakage. Any fringing drawing is qualitative, not a finite-element result.

claims.claim: In a mixed core-gap path, dividing total Ni by each separate segment length gives the wrong local field.
claims.equations: Hⱼ = Bⱼ/μⱼ; ΣHⱼlⱼ = Ni
claims.qualification: Ampere’s law remains valid; it is the full-loop balance, not an instruction to assign all MMF to every segment.

claims.claim: Reluctance depends on mean path length and the area normal to flux, including core depth.
claims.equations: A = depth × limb thickness; ℜtotal = Σlⱼ/(μⱼAⱼ)
claims.qualification: Mean core lengths exclude gap length. Example 1.4 directly supplies core length and must not have its gap subtracted again.

claims.claim: The same series flux can produce different flux densities in sections with different areas.
claims.equations: B₁ = Φ/A₁; B₂ = Φ/A₂
claims.qualification: In Example 1.2 the horizontal yokes have area 0.010 m²; the vertical limbs have area 0.015 m². Both are core, not air-gap sections.

claims.claim: In the interactive flux divider, common-limb flux divides between two return branches with equal branch MMF drop.
claims.equations: Φ = Φ₁ + Φ₂; Φ₁ℜ₁ = Φ₂ℜ₂; ℜeq = ℜc + ℜ₁ℜ₂/(ℜ₁+ℜ₂)
claims.qualification: This is an illustrative one-source network, distinct from the supplied two-source Example 1.3. Branch reluctances include their return yokes.

claims.claim: The lower-reluctance parallel path carries more flux. The divider follows from continuity and loop balance.
claims.equations: Φ₁ = Φℜ₂/(ℜ₁+ℜ₂); Φ₂ = Φℜ₁/(ℜ₁+ℜ₂)
claims.qualification: The supplied reluctances are positive, constant teaching values. There is no inferred cross section or measured material from the schematic geometry.

claims.claim: The supplied two-source Example 1.3 instead combines two loop fluxes through a shared gapped center limb.
claims.equations: Φg=Φ₁+Φ₂; (ℜo+ℜm)Φ₁+ℜmΦ₂=ℱ₁; ℜmΦ₁+(ℜo+ℜm)Φ₂=ℱ₂
claims.qualification: Here ℜm includes center-core plus gap reluctances. Corrected source arithmetic is recorded in the exercise audit.

claims.claim: A single winding in a fixed linear common-flux model has L=N²/ℜ.
claims.equations: λ = NΦ = Li; L = N²/ℜ
claims.qualification: L describes the winding/core system. It is not a separate property of the gap alone.

claims.claim: Induced emf opposes a change in linked flux; passive terminal voltage uses the corresponding positive derivative convention.
claims.equations: ℰ = −dλ/dt; v = dλ/dt = L di/dt for constant L
claims.qualification: Different sign conventions must not be mixed. Fixed DC current with fixed geometry does not produce a Faraday emf.

claims.claim: A linear inductor stores magnetic energy; in a gapped high-permeability structure a large share can be in the gap.
claims.equations: W = ½Li²; u = B²/(2μ) = BH/2; gap energy share = ℜg/(ℜc+ℜg) for equal-area series segments
claims.qualification: These formulas assume a reversible linear model. The gap-share expression follows by integrating energy density over each segment volume; it is 6/7≈85.7% for the stated inductor. With p=vi=dW/dt, negative power returns energy and a full ideal cycle has zero net transfer.

claims.claim: For a nonlinear linkage curve, a local derivative generally differs from the linkage-to-current ratio.
claims.equations: Ldiff = dλ/di; Lsec = λ/i
claims.qualification: This local distinction assumes a specified linkage-current curve or material state. It is not a complete model of arbitrary hysteresis history.

claims.claim: The two supplied series coils can aid or oppose according to their winding/current orientation.
claims.equations: ℱ = (Na ± Nb)i; Φ = (Na ± Nb)i/ℜ
claims.qualification: The series current is common. A signed flux-linkage convention is required for terminal inductance.

claims.claim: Self-inductance and mutual inductance separate the effects of each coil’s current.
claims.equations: La = Na²/ℜ; Lb = Nb²/ℜ; |M| = NaNb/ℜ; Lseries = La+Lb ± 2M = (Na ± Nb)²/ℜ
claims.qualification: These formulas use a linear, fully linked common-flux model. With both current references into the dots, λa=Laia+Mib and λb=Mia+Lbib. The course’s NaΦ/i under simultaneous excitation is a linkage/current ratio, not La in isolation.

claims.claim: Ferromagnetic materials are nonlinear and history-dependent; fixed μᵣ cannot be extrapolated through saturation.
claims.equations: Secant permeability B/H differs from incremental permeability dB/dH.
claims.qualification: The source’s 2.5 T and 3.9 T outputs follow ideal exercise assumptions, not a verified material curve.

claims.claim: Remanence and coercivity describe a hysteresis loop; loop area represents cycle loss per unit volume.
claims.equations: wcycle = ∮ H dB
claims.qualification: Any analytic curve in the lesson is explicitly schematic and is not fitted manufacturer data.

claims.claim: Thin insulated laminations constrain circulating currents and reduce eddy-current heating; this mechanism differs from hysteresis.
claims.equations: Changing magnetic flux induces currents; electrical resistance dissipates their energy.
claims.qualification: Sheet planes run parallel to the main flux. Current paths are schematic; no quantitative efficiency or core-loss estimate is displayed.

claims.claim: Real material specifications must identify test conditions rather than a universal saturation number.
claims.equations: Example only: N87 data depend on H, frequency and temperature.
claims.qualification: The linked TDK datasheet is an external evidence example. It is not the material used by the interactive models.

claims.claim: Examples 1.0–1.5 retain the supplied numerical inputs; all displayed solutions are recomputed in SI units.
claims.equations: See the calculation audit below.
claims.qualification: Small differences from the slides reflect unrounded arithmetic. Actual source errors are documented separately.

claims.claim: The five quiz answers follow the same cited equations and assumptions as the teaching sections.
claims.equations: 1: Same series Φ. 2: Lower gap permeability. 3: v=0 at a smooth sinusoidal-current peak. 4: Lseries=0 for equal perfectly coupled opposing turns. 5: Sum signed Hℓ drops.
claims.qualification: Questions test the stated ideal model. Ideal common-flux cancellation excludes real leakage inductance.

claims.claim: The electric-circuit bridge solves the original two-source network using KCL and checks each loop using KVL.
claims.qualification: The original lecture gives this circuit without a worked answer. The displayed solution is an independently checked completion of that problem.

examples.title: Symmetric two-window core with shared gapped center limb

geometry_read_from_figure.figure_dimension_unit: cm, inferred unambiguously from p28 conversions, although p27 figure does not explicitly print a unit legend
geometry_read_from_figure.flux_topology: Flux Phi1 enters center from left outer loop; Phi2 enters from right outer loop; center/gap flux is Phi1+Phi2. Both source polarities + toward top central node.

notes: P28 center-core reluctance is an arithmetic error: .515/(mu0×1200×.0004)=.853800e6 At/Wb, not .82e6.

P29 displayed coefficients follow the erroneous rounded .82e6 value, but its printed flux result is close to the correct unrounded geometry solution. Solve the corrected system, do not reuse 13.34e6/10.76e6.
Correct equations: (Router+Rcenter)Phi1+Rcenter Phi2=5000; Rcenter Phi1+(Router+Rcenter)Phi2=5000; Rcenter includes center-core plus gap.
Symmetry simplifies Phi1=Phi2=5000/(Router+2Rcenter). The effective circuit is not three reluctances all in series.

examples.title: Inductance of a gapped single-coil core
examples.geometry_read_from_figure: Source explicitly calls lc=.50 m mean core length; p32 uses .50 m directly in Rc. Do not subtract .001 m again.
notes: P32 B numerator prints .6463×10^-4 Wb but then reports .4309 T. Correct numerator is .6463×10^-3 Wb, consistent with its own L expression lower on page.
PPTX includes an isolated -3 text shape on slide32, suggesting an attempted correction; the rendered PDF still shows the incorrect -4 numerator. Use corrected arithmetic.
Question says inductance in the air gap. Inductance is a property of the coil/core magnetic system; B and H can be evaluated in the gap.

examples.title: Two series-connected coils, aiding and opposing

geometry_read_from_figure.diagram_dimension_unit: cm (depth label is 2 cm; other dimension numbers follow same unit)

notes: Source La=Na Phi/i and Lb=Nb Phi/i under simultaneous series excitation are flux-linkage/current ratios under that connection, not standalone self-inductances.

For ideal common-flux linear model, self La=Na²/R, self Lb=Nb²/R, M=Na Nb/R; Lseries=La+Lb±2M=(Na±Nb)²/R. For opposing connection terminal linkage has opposite sign for coil B; do not add unsigned ratios.
Source omits opposing inductance values. Series equivalent inductances here are checked extensions, requiring an external coupled-inductor source for new explanatory content.
3.9 T and target 3 T follow an imposed constant μr. No actual material curve is provided; do not suggest a practical core achieves these with μr=3000.
Rounded source Rg=3e6 is ≈0.53% above unrounded 2.984155e6. This explains slightly different inverse currents, not a formula error.

electric_review.orientation: Both voltage source positive terminals at top; i1 and i2 enter central top node, i3 exits downward through R3.
electric_review.note: Source page17 is unsolved. Calculated answer is a derived completion, not printed source result.

model_assumptions: Core relative permeability is held constant at the exercise-given value; calculated high B does not validate that approximation for a real unspecified material.
Uniform B across each segment area and H approximately uniform along each segment mean path.
Leakage flux neglected, and all relevant turns link the modeled flux.
Fringing neglected; effective air-gap area equals adjacent core face area.
Core path lengths exclude air gaps unless lc is explicitly given as mean core length (Example 1.4).
All calculations use SI units and unrounded intermediate quantities; source final answers often use rounded intermediates.

errata.resolution: Use 10⁴. Recomputed i for Φ=0.012 Wb is 2.015963 A. The requested H values are supplied by H=B/(μ₀μᵣ).

errata.issue: Center-core reluctance is printed as 0.82×10⁶ At/Wb, creating inconsistent loop coefficients.
errata.resolution: Use 0.853800×10⁶ At/Wb. Correct system diagonal/off-diagonal are 13.387252×10⁶ and 10.800984×10⁶ At/Wb. The gap flux is 0.413424 mWb.

errata.issue: The numerator in the B expression prints 0.6463×10⁻⁴ Wb.
errata.resolution: The correct exponent is −3, consistent with the source’s own inductance expression. B≈0.430847 T and L≈0.258508 H.

errata.issue: Individual NΦ/i ratios with both coils excited are labeled inductances, and the handout rejects N²/ℜ too broadly.
errata.resolution: Distinguish self-inductance, mutual inductance and series equivalent inductance. With ideal common flux, Lseries=(Na±Nb)²/ℜ.

errata.issue: The handout says not to use Ampere’s law for local H.
errata.resolution: Ampere’s law still governs the complete loop. The invalid step is assigning the total MMF independently to each segment.

errata.issue: H is called “magnetic field density”; the exercise asks for “inductance in the air gap.”
errata.resolution: Use magnetic field intensity for H. Inductance belongs to the winding/core system; B and H may be evaluated in the gap.

errata.issue: Fixed-permeability calculations give high B without an identified real core material.
errata.resolution: Retain the exercise result but identify the constant-μᵣ approximation. Do not treat it as a practical unsaturated operating prediction.

claims.knowledge: At a junction Φtotal = Φ1 + Φ2. For parallel return paths, Φ1 R1 = Φ2 R2. For each complete loop, NI = Φtotal Rc + Φbranch Rbranch.
The equivalent reluctance is Rc + R1 R2/(R1+R2); the inverse-reluctance flux divider follows from continuity and equal branch MMF drop.
claims.classification: Algebraic consequence of the cited network laws

claims.knowledge: Each local B is branch flux divided by local cross section; local H = B/μ only for the assumed linear medium.
Both currents referenced into corresponding dots produce reinforcing common-path flux. Series-aiding uses B1-to-A2; series-opposing B1-to-B2 with the shown fixed physical dot positions.
For a linear common path with no leakage, L1=N1²/R, L2=N2²/R and M=N1N2/R. Thus Lseries = L1+L2±2M = (N1±N2)²/R.
claims.classification: Derived from cited equations under stated perfect-coupling assumptions

claims.knowledge: For dotted-current references λ1 = L1 i1 + M i2 and λ2 = M i1 + L2 i2. λ1/i1 with both coils excited is generally not L1. In the series model, λseries=(N1±N2)Φ and Lseries is defined by its linear coefficient even when i=0.
claims.classification: Superposition and terminal linkage; corrects the source handout's overbroad λ/i instruction

models.title: Three-limb flux divider
models.parameter_origin: Explicit illustrative teaching values chosen to expose flux division, not copied measurements or specifications of a manufactured core.
assumptions: Constant linear positive reluctances
Leakage omitted
Each return branch's reluctance includes its corresponding yoke portions
Core picture is schematic and is not used to infer physical dimensions or permeability
checks: Across the slider sweep, total-left-right ≈ 0 and NI-total*Rc-branch*Rbranch ≈ 0 for each loop. Rounded node values use ≈ in the visible display.
models.visual_semantics: Arrows are stationary chevrons with pulsing opacity. No material particles are drawn. Width/opacity compare flux, not physical speed or conductor current. Core center arrows point up and outer arrows point down.

models.title: Series-aiding/opposing coils on a common core
models.parameter_origin: Turn counts mirror the lecture's two-winding illustration; reluctance and current range are explicitly teaching values. This is not the lecture's high-flux-density numerical geometry or a measured device.
assumptions: Linear, stationary magnetic system
A single common flux links every turn of both coils
No leakage; k=1
No winding resistance, core saturation or hysteresis
Positive series current enters A1. Dot currents are i1=i and i2=s*i
Positive common flux is clockwise in the drawing
checks: At zero current, flux/linkage and both MMFs are zero; inductance is still 250 mH or 40 mH, with no division by zero.
Reversing current reverses flux, linkage and both MMFs while leaving inductance positive and unchanged.
Series linkage equals λ1+s*λ2; Lseries equals L1+L2+2*s*M.
models.visual_semantics: The physical windings and their dotted A terminals stay fixed. The circuit reverses the displayed terminal order of coil 2 when switching to opposing. Positive current entering A rises in the dashed back-side winding segment, then descends in the bright front-side segment. Downward front-side current across the horizontal top limb gives a rightward field along that limb and clockwise core flux. With x right, y up and z toward the viewer, the current circulation tangent at the front is x-hat cross z-hat = minus y-hat, consistent with the right-hand rule. Upper arrows are explicitly labeled MMF directions; the loop arrows show the net field direction. All arrows indicate directions, not field transport.

materials-models.json.curveStatus: Original normalized schematic drawing, not measured data, not fitted to a material, and not a predictive hysteresis simulation.

initialMagnetization.physicalRole: Qualitative first magnetization from a demagnetized state, showing diminishing response at high excitation. No units or material values are assigned.

hysteresis.drawingParameter: p ranges from 0 to 1 along a complete illustrative major loop; t=2 pi p
hysteresis.drawingCoordinates: h=-cos(t); branch=+1 for sin(t)>=0 and -1 otherwise; offset=0.34 branch (1-h^2); b=[0.92 tanh(2.5(h-offset))+0.08h]/[0.92 tanh(2.5)+0.08]
hysteresis.physicalRole: Lower branch from negative to positive excitation; upper branch on return. At p=0.75, h=0 and b is positive. The negative coercive-field label is numerically located at the descending-branch zero crossing.
hysteresis.limits: No predicted minor loops, actual Hc, Br, Bs, loss, temperature response, or frequency response. The phase slider traverses a specified geometric path; it does not solve arbitrary history-dependent magnetization.
hysteresis.shownPhysicalFormula: The dimensional physical loop area integral H dB is energy loss per unit volume per cycle. No number is calculated from the normalized drawing.

eddyCurrents.construction: Schematic cross section perpendicular to the main flux. Main B points into/out of the screen, parallel to sheet planes. Insulation appears as narrow gaps between vertical sheets.
eddyCurrents.laminated: Nine separate sheet-local paths; no current crosses insulating boundaries.
eddyCurrents.excitation: For visual timing only, main B sign follows sin(phase), current visibility follows abs(cos(phase)), and dash motion reverses with the flux derivative. No field amplitude or frequency in physical units is assigned.
eddyCurrents.limits: No solved current density, temperature, dissipation or efficiency. Edge effects, skin effect, and interlaminar faults are not modeled.
